Issued at 154 AM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

             -----------Synoptic Overview-----------

Deep-layer southerly flow persists over the Florida Peninsula early
this morning. Low pressure associated with the remnants of Isaias
sits near Chattanooga, TN, with a cold front extending into the NE
Gulf. This continues to funnel unseasonably high moisture over the
area, with PWAT values in excess of 2.3". Over the next 24 hours,
this disturbance will slowly move eastward, with its attendant
cold front arriving over Central Florida this afternoon. By Monday
morning, it should exit to the south of the district.

Unusually strong high pressure at H5 sits over the Western Atlantic,
with heights over 597 dam near Bermuda. As the shortwave trough
associated with Isaias moves into the Atlantic, this ridge will
flatten, and another strong anticyclone will replace it over the
Gulf by Monday. Weak northwesterly flow will force much drier air
over Florida through at least early Wednesday.

By mid-week, an inverted trough is forecast to be passing through
the NW Caribbean Sea. Strong high pressure should still be
located over the Deep South. East-southeasterly flow in the lower
troposphere will begin to advect moisture back over the southern
half of the state during the second half of the week. Guidance
has shifted earlier and farther north with the return of near-
to above-normal moisture, particularly from Thursday into Friday.

The ensemble suite continues to struggle to resolve the mid-latitude
pattern late this week and into next weekend. This seems to stem
from the interaction between a cut-off low over the southern Rockies
and a polar jet streak diving out of the Canadian Prairies. GEFS 
members strongly phase these features, digging an unseasonably 
deep trough into the Ohio Valley by Saturday. The EPS suite shows 
less phasing, with the northern stream carving out a broader 
trough over the Northeast U.S. Cluster analysis of the 10/12Z 
guidance showed a nearly 50/50 split in outcomes, but the early- 
arriving 11/00Z guidance has trended more toward a phased 
solution. For Florida, more phasing and a stronger trough would 
send a cold front toward the state by Saturday.

             -------Sensible Weather & Impacts-------

Through Tonight...

With a convergent stream of tropical moisture focusing over
Central Florida, we will continue to see numerous showers and a
few storms. A few storms may produce wind gusts from 40-50 mph
today. Where repeated rounds of heavy rain occur, we will monitor
for localized flooding due to already saturated soil. Looking at
the 95th percentile of the REFS members, areas from Cape Canaveral
to southern Osceola County and points southward stand the highest
chance of locally excessive rain through this evening. In this area,
there is a 5-10% chance of rainfall amounts exceeding 3".

The weak cold front approaches the I-4 corridor by late this
afternoon. It should then slowly work southward, reaching Lake
Okeechobee before daybreak on Monday. Somewhat less humid air will
quickly suppress rain chances once it passes your location. Some
low shower chances linger tonight mainly near Lake O and along
the Treasure Coast.

Highs today remain above normal over the Treasure Coast, in the
upper 80s to low 90s. Elsewhere, highs reach the mid to upper
80s. Tonight's low temps will turn a bit cooler to the north of
the front, with upper 60s to near 70 along I-4 and low to mid 70s
southward from there.

Monday - Tuesday...

A break from the wet weather arrives to begin the work week. Much
drier air will mix to the surface on Monday afternoon, allowing
dew points to drop into the mid 60s to near 70. Under mostly sunny
skies, highs will still be warm in the mid to upper 80s. Widespread
mid to upper 60s are expected for lows Monday night, except low
70s right along the immediate coast south of Melbourne.

Some boundary-layer moisture returns from the Atlantic on
Tuesday. While a few sprinkles are possible, the most likely
outcome is just some intervals of cloud cover. Seasonably warm
temps prevail in the afternoon.

Wednesday - Friday...

As moderate onshore flow commences, one notable change is an
earlier return of sufficient moisture for a few showers during the
second half of the work week. Through Thursday, these chances range
from 20-40% generally south of Orlando before increasing to 30-50%
area-wide on Friday. Lightning probabilities look quite low through
at least Thursday.

Partly sunny skies should continue, with high temps near to just
above normal in the mid to upper 80s.

Next Weekend...

Uncertainty grows as we monitor multiple disturbances and their
potential impact on our local weather. As mentioned in the overview,
a trough over the Ohio Valley and/or Northeast may drag a cold
front toward the state or reinforce high pressure to our north. A
stronger front could draw deeper moisture northward, increasing
chances for showers and storms as it does. It's too early to
tell for certain. St
